patch.value: Removing the cmd.exe launch would close the shell-command alert, but the obvious version of that change breaks Windows

CodeQL alert 2 reports js/shell-command-constructed-from-input at index.ts line 1120, where the win32 branch of pmLaunchPlan builds a single command tail for cmd.exe by joining the binary path and every pm argument. The message is accurate: a string concatenation that depends on library input is later used in a shell command.

The existing code is not careless about it. quoteWindowsArg applies the documented CommandLineToArgvW escaping so every metacharacter cmd honours inside quotes is neutralised, the tail is outer-quoted so cmd's /s handling strips exactly the pair we added, and assertNoCmdVariableExpansion refuses the launch outright when an argument contains a %NAME% pair, because cmd expands those even inside quotes with no escape available. That last defence exists specifically so a workspace path containing %BUILD% cannot make pm silently read a different workspace and report success.

The clean way to close the alert is to stop using a command processor at all: resolve the shim to the JS entry it wraps and spawn node with that entry and discrete argv elements, which removes the string concatenation rather than escaping it. An attempt at this was drafted and rejected, and the reason is worth recording so the next attempt does not repeat it. The draft made the direct spawn unconditional, which breaks the case the cmd.exe path exists for: npm writes three shims into node_modules/.bin, on Windows only the .cmd is executable, and Node refuses to spawn a .cmd directly with EINVAL. A launch plan that cannot resolve a JS entry must therefore still have a command processor to fall back to, so the alert does not disappear — it only stops being on the path that normally runs.

Deliberately not dismissed. Dismissing would require arguing the quoting is complete, and the honest position is that the mitigations are careful but unverified, which is exactly the claim a scanner is better placed to doubt than a reviewer.

The normal launch path resolves the shim to its JS entry and spawns node with discrete argv elements, with no command string built anywhere on it; the cmd.exe fallback is retained only for the case where no JS entry can be resolved, and a test asserts that a .cmd shim with no resolvable entry still launches rather than failing EINVAL; and CodeQL either closes alert 2 or the remaining fallback is dismissed with the reachability argument written on the alert
